editorial_examples.note: The source used an outdated spelling and a passive verb clause, while this entry is the adjective geladen. Replaced it with a current, direct adjectival example.

editorial_examples.german: Die Rakete zog wie ein Komet über den Himmel.
editorial_examples.english: The rocket streaked across the sky like a comet.
editorial_examples.note: The German does not specify a weapon, so “rocket” is more accurate than “missile” in this context.

editorial_examples.german: Wie findet ihr mein neues Kostüm?
editorial_examples.english: What do you think of my new skirt suit?
editorial_examples.note: Made the English gloss specific to the skirt-suit sense of Kostüm rather than the broader word “suit.”

editorial_examples.german: Die Media bildet die mittlere Schicht der Gefäßwand.
editorial_examples.english: The tunica media forms the middle layer of the vessel wall.
editorial_examples.note: The source used Medien (mass media), which is a different word and sense. Replaced it with an example of the technical anatomical noun Media.

editorial_examples.german: Der Sender überträgt das Konzert live.
editorial_examples.english: The station broadcasts the concert live.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a broad medical claim about leeches with a neutral example of übertragen meaning to transmit/broadcast.

editorial_examples.german: Wann habt ihr das letzte Mal ein Kompliment bekommen?
editorial_examples.english: When was the last time you received a compliment?
editorial_examples.note: Corrected the German spelling and spacing in das letzte Mal.

editorial_examples.german: Er ist der Benjamin der Familie.
editorial_examples.english: He is the youngest child in the family.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate referred to Benjamin Franklin, a proper name unrelated to the noun Benjamin meaning the youngest child in a family. Replaced it with the common noun sense.

editorial_examples.german: Bitte füllen Sie die Flasche mit Wasser.
editorial_examples.english: Please fill the bottle with water.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a dated fuel-grade example with a simple, current example of füllen.

editorial_examples.german: Tom erschien nach seiner Freilassung auf Kaution nicht zur Gerichtsverhandlung.
editorial_examples.english: Tom did not appear at the trial after his release on bail.
editorial_examples.note: Improved the German phrasing and translated the sentence directly rather than using the separate English idiom “jumped bail.”

editorial_examples.german: Du weißt schon, dass ich dich jetzt festnehmen könnte, oder?
editorial_examples.english: You do realize that I could arrest you right now, don’t you?
editorial_examples.note: Corrected the outdated spelling daß to dass and refreshed the English to sound natural.

editorial_examples.english: The patient suffered a heart attack.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a sentence implying a particular activity caused a heart attack with a neutral medical example.

editorial_examples.german: Die Tragödie des Stücks wird erst im letzten Akt deutlich.
editorial_examples.english: The tragedy of the play becomes clear only in the final act.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced the contradictory description of a tragedy with a happy ending with a clear, natural example of Tragödie.

editorial_examples.german: Bei Hunden gibt es viele verschiedene Rassen.
editorial_examples.english: There are many different breeds of dogs.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced the outdated, potentially misleading application of Rasse to humans with a clear animal-breed use.

editorial_examples.german: Nach dem Abschied überkam ihn großer Kummer.
editorial_examples.english: After the farewell, great sorrow came over him.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced an unnecessarily distressing story about violent death with a neutral example of Kummer.
